sections.title: 0. Changes vs. the previous edition
sections.html:
This event is not an action by Berkshire the company but a transfer of shares by a major shareholder personally. Buffett converted 6,150 Class A shares into Class B shares and donated them to four family foundations. Berkshire's equity, cash, A-share-equivalent share count and BPS do not change (the conversion is an A↔B exchange, not a new share issuance or a cash movement — judgment). What changed is voting-power concentration (29.7% → 29.6%) and economic ownership (13.2% → 12.9%). From the same measurement-layer list, we also read five 13Gs that the previous edition had not read, and among them Bending Spoons' ownership of 6.4% (9/30) fills one blank in T5. Probabilities and the assumed value band do not move — no rule was triggered.

Source: the two original filings above. Total gifts of 9,225,000 shares = number of shares converted (formula 3,690,000 + 1,845,000 × 3).

  • Holdings after the transactions (13D/A No. 82 cover page): 182,140 Class A shares (38.4% of Class A) · 1,162 Class B shares (below 0.01%) · sole voting and dispositive power over all, shared 0 · voting power 29.6% · economic interest 12.9% (source: No. 82).
  • What the filing does not give: the value at the time of the gifts. Approximated with the 2026-11-16 Class B closing price, it is about $5.47 billion (estimate — formula 9,225,000 × 592.85; closing price from stockanalysis).
  • On the same day, 'Thanksgiving Message from Warren Buffett' (2026-11-16) was posted on the Berkshire website (source: 2026 press release list). This probe could not read the PDF text — since statements in the letter are not judgment material in the first place (Rule 1), recording milestone candidates is also deferred to the next issue.
Reproducing the Cover-Page Numbers (Cross-Check)
  • Class A 38.4%: subtracting this conversion's 6,150 shares from the 480,476 Class A shares on the 10-Q cover (2026-10-28) gives 474,326 shares → 182,140 ÷ 474,326 = 38.4% (formula; cover page from the 10-Q). Other conversions between 10/28 and 11/16 could not be reflected (estimate).
  • Economic interest 12.9%: 182,140 ÷ 1,416,346 Class A-equivalent shares (10-Q cover) = 12.86% (formula) — conversion does not change the total Class A-equivalent count.
  • Voting power 29.6%: one Class B share carries 1/10,000 of the voting power of a Class A share (definition — state.definitions.buffett_stake). 1,413,030,594 Class B shares (formula 1,403,805,594 + 9,225,000) ÷ 10,000 = 141,303 votes + 474,326 Class A votes = 615,629 votes → 182,140 ÷ 615,629 = 29.6% (formula).

Sources: No. 80(2025-11-12) · No. 81(2026-07-15) · No. 82(2026-11-17).

  • Over one year (No. 80 → No. 82), A shares fell by 14,177 (−7.2%, formula (196,317 − 182,140) ÷ 196,317), yet voting power fell only 0.2%p (same source). Reason (judgment): other A-share holders also converted A shares into B shares, so the total number of A shares shrank as well, and the share within A shares actually rose from 37.7% to 38.4% — since a B share carries 1/10,000 of the vote, voting power is determined almost entirely by the A-share ratio.
  • The economic stake fell from 13.6% to 12.9%, down 0.7%p (same source) — more than three times faster than voting power (formula 0.7 ÷ 0.2).
  • Between No. 80 and No. 81, A shares fell by 27 more than the 8,000 converted (formula 196,317 − 8,000 − 188,290). Presumed to be a minor movement between the two amendments — the cause could not be confirmed.
  • 2026 cumulative (No. 81 + No. 82): 14,150 A shares converted · 21,225,000 shares donated as Class B (formula 8,000 + 6,150 · 12,000,000 + 9,225,000).

sections.title: 3. What Reaches Berkshire (the Company) — Axis E · Disruptive Variable D6
sections.html:
• Equity, BPS, share count: No change — a conversion merely exchanges 1 Class A share for 1,500 Class B shares and does not change the total A-equivalent count of 1,416,346 shares (10-Q cover 2026-10-28) (formula 6,150 × 1,500 ÷ 1,500 = 6,150 A-equivalent remains, source: Form 4 footnote '1:1,500 conversion').
  • Class B float supply: The donated 9,225,000 shares are 0.66% of the Class B shares on the 10-Q cover (formula 9,225,000 ÷ 1,403,805,594) and 0.43% of the total A-equivalent count (formula 6,150 ÷ 1,416,346). When the foundation disposes of these shares is not addressed by the 13D or Form 4 (the foundation is not a reporting party — judgment).
  • Governance (D6): A single individual's 29.6% voting power remains the largest (source: 82nd). No determination changes because of this filing — Axis E milestones E-2027-1 (relative share price) and E-2028-1 (wildfire losses) do not measure voting power. Changes in voting structure are an observation target of master Axis E but are not yet defined as a milestone — this edition creates no new milestone or rule and only records the definition (state.definitions.buffett_stake) and the time series.
  • Probability adjustment rules: None of R1~R6 is conditioned on a major shareholder's stake (source: state.probability_adjustment_rules) — probabilities 25/50/25 maintained.

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.html:
• One-sentence conclusion: On 2026-11-16 Buffett gifted 6,150 Class A shares (9,225,000 Class B shares) to four family foundations, bringing his voting power to 29.6% and economic interest to 12.9%, but Berkshire's equity, BPS and share count are unchanged, and on the same day a 13G disclosed for the first time a 6.4% stake in Bending Spoons — the 25/50/25 probabilities and the assumed value band are unchanged (Sources: 13D/A No. 82 · 13G).
  • Briefing in 5 lines
  • Buffett 13D/A No. 82 (2026-11-16): 6,150 Class A shares → converted into 9,225,000 Class B shares, then gifted to four family foundations (roughly $5.47 billion, estimated at the 11/16 closing price)(13D/A).
  • After the transaction: 182,140 Class A shares · voting power 29.6% (29.7% in July) · economic interest 12.9% (13.2% in July)(same source · No. 81).
  • Conversion does not change the Class A-equivalent share count or BPS — the gifted amount is 0.66% of Class B shares outstanding (formula).
  • 13G (2026-11-16): Bending Spoons 6.4% · Delta 9.8% · Bank of America 6.6% · VeriSign 6.6% · Kroger 5.9% (9/30)(Bending Spoons 13G).
  • No rules R1–R6 met — scenarios 25/50/25 and assumed value band $265.0–$684.5 maintained · Class B closing price on 11/17: $586.76(stockanalysis).
  • Three data points to check directly before the next issue
  • Bending Spoons initial stake and acquisition cost — is the 6.4% (9/30) the value after settlement of the 'additional stake' (T5, 13G · 4Q26 10-K).
  • Whether Delta stake rises from 9.8% past 10% — 13G amendment · Form 4 (T3, Delta 13G).
  • Yen bond settlement (2026-11-19) and ¥73.4 billion maturity repayment (2026-11-27) — 4Q26 10-K debt note (T2, 424B5).
